sample_unit: consultation cases (three medical datasets; count not reported)
models_evaluated: 27 confidence estimation methods (token-level, consistency-level, linguistic self-assessment)

links.outcome: Reliability of LLM confidence estimates in multi-turn medical consultation as information accumulates
links.effect: Medical data amplifies the limitations of token-level and consistency-level confidence methods across 27 methods. The proposed MedConf outperformed state-of-the-art methods on AUROC and Pearson correlation across two LLMs and three datasets, including under information insufficiency.
links.quote: We implement and compare 27 representative methods on this benchmark; two key insights emerge: (1) medical data amplifies the inherent limitations of token-level and consistency-level confidence methods, and (2) medical reasoning must be evaluated for both diagnostic accuracy and information completeness.

unlisted_practices: Evidence-grounded, retrieval-augmented linguistic self-assessment to estimate LLM diagnostic confidence
Benchmarking confidence against an information sufficiency gradient in multi-turn consultations

screen.reason: The paper benchmarks confidence estimation methods and tests a retrieval-grounded linguistic self-assessment framework (MedConf) as a safeguard to accurately estimate LLM confidence/uncertainty during multi-turn medical consultation.

primary.practice: retrieval-grounded confidence estimation and uncertainty quantification
